slides.h1: Same Task, Different Hour: Why Timing Changes the Result
slides.sub: Hora (the planetary hour) is a classical way to match the work to the hour.

slides.body: Hora is a planetary hour: each day is split into hours ruled in sequence by the seven classical planets. The day's first hour belongs to the day lord.

slides.h2: Venus Hora: creative and design work
slides.body: Venus (Shukra) is the planet of aesthetics and harmony. Its hour is a traditional pick for design, writing, music and anything where taste matters.
Mars (Mangala) rules drive, muscle and effort. Its hour suits workouts, tough chores and tasks that need raw energy and push.

slides.h2: Why this works as a habit tool
slides.body: A fixed pairing removes a daily decision. You stop asking when to train or when to design, and the hour answers it for you.

points: Look up Hora times for your city's sunrise
Use the pairing for two weeks
Log energy and output, not mood
Keep it only if your own data agrees

slides.body: Hora is a tradition, not a laboratory result. Treat it as a scheduling experiment. It is not medical advice or a guarantee of performance.
